newsitem.title: USA: Colo issuer files brief in Moody's rating case.
newsitem.headline: Colo issuer files brief in Moody's rating case.

text.p: A U.S. district court in April ignored key First Amendment principles in barring Colorado's largest school district from sueing Moody's Investors Service on anti-trust charges, school district lawyers told an appeals panel Monday.
The law firm of Caplan and Earnest outlined the argument in a brief filed with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit on behalf of the Jefferson County School District.

The school district originally filed a three-count lawsuit in October 1995, alleging that Moody's committed "fraud, malice and willful and wanton conduct" when it issued an unsolicited opinion right before the district priced a $110.3 million refunding in 1993.
Then last year, the school district asked the court to hear two new counts alleging that Moody's violated the Sherman Act, the federal government's anti-monopoly law.
U.S. District Judge William Downes on April 8 dismissed the first three claims and denied the school district's motion to add the Sherman Act claims. The schools appealed April 4.
Downes conceded in his April 8 ruling that his decision was "harsh" but it "vastly outweighed" the "calamity" that would result if rating agencies were "muzzled into silence."
But the school district said Monday that Downes ignored a fundamental principle of First Amendment law.
"There is a long and unbroken line of cases holding that violations of the Sherman Act executed through speech are not protected by the First Amendment," the district said.
The court also ignored another key legal principle, the school district said: Illegal conduct does not become legal just because it is carried out through speech.
And school district lawyers noted that the "lynchpin" of the district court's holding was that there is something called "constitutionally protected opinion."
But that, the school district said, is a concept used in defamation law, not antitrust cases.
The case is Jefferson County School District v. Moody's Investors Service (Case No. 97-1157).
